description: Dry-run an import of a whole list — the product's own importer, the same one the app's import screen uses — and write NOTHING. Send the rows you built from your user's file (cells as strings, header row left out) and one `columns` entry per cell position with its target: name, description, category, homeLocation, currentLocation, responsiblePerson, currentHolder, blueprintName (an item model, by name), container (the item this row's item sits in — a vehicle, case or cart, named by the name or code of ANOTHER ROW of this file or of an existing item; a vehicle is an item with its own row, never a location), compartment (its compartment, e.g. «GR1», «Fahrerhaus»; created on the container when it is missing — only names from your user's file), code (a printed code or serial — the lasting way to tell identical pieces apart), quantity / minStock (stock items), trackingMode (quantity, menge, stückzahl, stueckzahl, bestand, pool (stock: a count of identical pieces) or serialized, serialisiert, einzeln, einzelstück, einzelstueck, unit (single pieces); a quantity or minStock value alone already makes a stock item), status, a fieldDefId from get_item_requirements or "field:<label>"; null skips a column. Categories and locations are matched by name and paths use `separator` ("Fahrzeuge/Anhänger"); create categories and fields first — anything listed under toCreate would be created by the import itself, which usually means a typo. Dates as "YYYY-MM-DD" or "DD.MM.YYYY" only: other forms are dropped (see problems). Rows without a code are matched to existing items BY NAME, so every code-less name must be unique in the file (one stock article in several places aside, below) — suffix duplicates the way your user's file does («Helm TLF», «Helm KLF»). Single items are packed into their container; a stock row's count goes into it. One stock article in several places: one row per place, all with the SAME name — and the same code, if it has one — each with its own container, compartment and count; at most one of them without a container, whose count is the stock at the item's home. They become ONE stock item: the dry run shows the row without a container (else the first) as create and the others as place, and lists each article's places and total under stockGroups. Identical single pieces are not grouped — give each its own name or code. The result says per row what would be created, updated or skipped, every value that would be dropped and why, what would be placed in which container and compartment and which compartments would be created, blockers that must be fixed first, columns the organization's plan cannot import, and whether the import lands past the plan's item allowance (allowed ONCE: after that no item can be added until the organization upgrades — tell your user before they confirm). Show your user the outcome, including what will not come in, and get ONE explicit OK; then call run_import with the SAME arguments and the returned planHash. At most 1000 rows per call; a longer list goes into the app's import screen as a CSV you write. entity "persons" or "locations" imports people or places instead (targets: name, parentPath, email). Requires the manager role to run, any member to plan.

columns.description: One entry per cell position of a row, in the same order

header.description: The column's header as in the file

target.description: Import target (see the tool description), a field definition id, "field:<label>", or null to skip the column

fileName.description: Your user's file name (shown in the app's import history), e.g. Inventar 2024.xlsx

keepOrder.description: Items are imported last row first by default, so the file's first row is the newest item and the app's list opens on it; true keeps the file order

rows.description: The data rows you built from your user's file, cells as strings, header row left out. At most 1000 rows per call

separator.description: Path separator in category and location cells (default "/": "Fahrzeuge/Anhänger")

name: plan_import

blockers.description: What run_import refuses until it is fixed. Empty = none

detail.description: What is wrong and how to fix it

kind.description: duplicateNameWithoutCode, duplicateCode, placementGroupTooLarge, duplicateUniqueValue, unknownField, ambiguousField, unknownTarget, duplicateTarget, noNameColumn, noCategoryColumn, rowTooWide, noRows, overCap

rows.description: 1-based positions in the rows you sent

capacity.description: The plan's item allowance; null = no allowance

columnsNotImported.description: Mapped columns the organization's plan cannot import

order.description: reversed (default for items: the first row becomes the newest item, so the app's list opens on it) or "file" (keepOrder)

placements.description: Only with a container column: per container, the single items packed into it and the stock counts that go into it

compartmentsToCreate.description: Compartments the import adds to it, in the file's order

existingItemId.description: Set when the container is an existing item

planChanged.description: run_import only: nothing was written, the plan changed

planHash.description: Pass to run_import with the SAME arguments; it changes when the rows or the organization's answers change

problems.description: Every row that does not simply create an item cleanly: dropped values, skipped rows, updates of existing items

code.description: The importer's issue code, e.g. invalidValue (the value is dropped), missingCategory (row skipped), containerNotFound (the row imports unplaced)

placesIntoRow.description: A stock article's row: the 1-based row of the item it adds its count to

refused.description: Set when the call was refused and nothing was written: tooManyRows, tooManyColumns, blockers, batchUndone

stockGroups.description: Only with a container column: each stock article whose rows (one per place, same name and code) become ONE stock item — its total, the pieces at home and per place

homePieces.description: Pieces at the item's home location

row.description: 1-based position of the row that defines the item

summary.description: Rows by outcome: create / update / skip / place (adds stock in a place to another row's item, see stockGroups), and by status: ok / warnings (the row imports, a value is dropped) / errors (the row is skipped)

toCreate.description: What the import itself would create by name — usually a typo when you created the structure first

compartments.description: «Container › compartment» per compartment the import adds

title: Plan an import (dry run)
